-- ===== MANAGER: main program =====
-- What it is for: turn the customer's orders into "keep this many of each item in stock" tables, and
-- act as the watchdog for all other boards.
-- Startup: read settings + orders from the databank; for each ordered item look up its recipe
-- (system.getRecipes), pick the recipe, and compute how many of every ingredient must be kept in stock:
--   builds      = the ordered items                       -> databank key "chef"
--   ingredients = their direct ingredients (x line multipliers) -> key "waitress"
--   ingredients = the full ingredient tree                 -> key "linecook"
-- line_mins = minimum stock for some common items; special rules scale stock for luminescent glass/LEDs
-- and honeycomb pures. Then two timers start: `buttonsOn` (switch boards on) and `next` (watchdog).
-- WATCHDOG: each board writes ping:<name>; the manager has one manual switch per board, named exactly like
-- the board. A stale ping (> 30 s) -> `next` turns that switch off once; `buttonsOn` turns it on again later.
-- HOW TINY FACTORY (TF) WORKS, in one paragraph
--   customer (settings + orders) -> databank <- manager (recipes -> what to keep in stock, watchdog)
--   -> chef / linecook / waitress boards (this program) -> the industry machines linked to them.
--   Boards only talk through databank keys. A cook board's role is its name minus a trailing digit
--   (chef, linecook1 -> "linecook", waitress). The manager's watchdog restarts a board whose
--   `ping:<name>` key goes stale. See my private DECISIONS.md notes for the full story and the reasons for every change.

-- PB_MANAGER.LUA

-- [MEM DEC-009] RESTART BACKOFF. Old: a board whose ping went stale was switched off and `buttonsOn` switched it
-- straight back on a few seconds later, every time. When the chef dies at startup that is a restart storm: each
-- restart is a memory burst in the shared pool that can kill the next board. New: the first failure holds the board
-- off for 30 s, the second in a row for 60 s, the third and later for 120 s. A board counts as healthy again once
-- it has run 120 s past the end of its last hold with a fresh ping.
--   restart_fails[name] = failures in a row;  hold_until[name] = time before which buttonsOn must leave it off.
restart_fails = {}
hold_until = {}

function next() 
    time = math.floor(system.getArkTime())

    -- [MEM DEC-008] Also publish this board's Lua heap size (KB) as mem:<board>, so memory can be measured
    -- in game instead of guessed. Read it with the databank, or watch chat with tf_debug = true.
    local kb = math.floor(collectgarbage("count"))
    databank.setIntValue("mem:manager", kb)
    if tf_debug then
        local line = "heap KB manager=" .. kb
        for name, _ in pairs(buttons) do line = line .. " " .. name .. "=" .. databank.getIntValue("mem:" .. name) end
        system.print(line)
    end

    --out("status checking... ", time)
    for name, slot in pairs(buttons) do
        local timeping = databank.getIntValue("ping:" .. name)
        if (time - timeping) > 30 then
            -- turn it OFF once; buttonsOn will re-enable later
            local a = slot.isActive()
            if a == 1 or a == true then
                slot.deactivate()
                databank.clearValue("status:" .. name)
                restart_fails[name] = (restart_fails[name] or 0) + 1
                local wait = math.min(30 * 2 ^ (restart_fails[name] - 1), 120)
                hold_until[name] = time + math.floor(wait)
                out("toggling", name)
                return
            end
        elseif hold_until[name] and (time - hold_until[name]) > 120 then
            -- fresh ping and well past the last hold: the board is healthy again, forget its failures
            restart_fails[name] = nil
            hold_until[name] = nil
        end
    end

end

function getIngredients(items, base, recurse)
    local new = false

    if base == nil then base = {} end
    local ingredients = base
    if recurse then ingredients = items end

    repeat
        new = false
        for _, item in pairs(items) do
            local item_id = item.id

            -- determine what we will need to build the item
            local recipes = system.getRecipes(item_id)
            local inputs, recipe = getPrimaryIngredients(item_id, recipes)

            local time_multiplier = 1

            -- [FIX DEC-014] Old: `if recipes and recipes[1] then local recipe = recipes[1]` - the inputs came from the
            -- recipe that makes the most of the item, but the time (used to size the stock) came from the FIRST recipe in
            -- the list. For an item with several recipes the two could belong to different recipes. New: `recipe` is the
            -- one the inputs come from.
            if recipe then
                time_multiplier = math.ceil(300 / recipe.time) -- lua recipe.time is base time, but skills might allow you to make much more in less time, try to accomodate this

                for _, input_item in pairs(inputs) do
                    if ignore_list[item.id] ~= true then
                        if ingredients[input_item.id] == nil then 
                            ingredients[input_item.id] = {id= input_item.id, quantity= 0}
                            new = true
                        end

                        quantity = math.ceil(math.max(input_item.quantity * time_multiplier, ingredients[input_item.id].quantity))
                        if recurse == false then quantity = math.ceil(quantity  * line_multiplier / num_lines) end
                        if line_mins[input_item.id] then 
                            quantity = math.max(line_mins[input_item.id], quantity)
                        end

                        -----
                        local tName = string.lower(getName(item.id))
                        if tName == nil then tName = "-=-" end
                        local boostLevel = 3.42
                        local ms, me = tName:find("luminescent")
                        if ms then
                            local iiName = string.lower(getName(input_item.id))  
                            local ms2, me2 = iiName:find("advanced glass") 
                            if ms2 then
                                quantity = math.ceil(quantity * boostLevel)
                                --system.print(" >>> debug >>> " .. tName .. ":" .. iiName .. ":" .. ingredients[input_item.id].quantity .. "=>" .. quantity)
                                end
                            local ms2, me2 = iiName:find("led") 
                            if ms2 then
                                quantity = math.ceil(quantity * boostLevel)
                                --system.print(" >>> debug >>> " .. tName .. ":" .. iiName .. ":" .. ingredients[input_item.id].quantity .. "=>" .. quantity)
                                end
                            end
                            
                        hcTypes = {"aged", "galvanized", "glossy", "matte", "painted", "panel", "pattern", "polished", "stained"}
                        hcPures = {"aluminium"}   
                        for _, hcType in pairs(hcTypes) do
                            local ms, me = tName:find(string.lower(hcType))
                            local ofConcern = false
                            for _, hcPure in pairs(hcPures) do
                               local ms1, me1 = tName:find(string.lower(hcPure))
                                    if ms1 then ofConcern = true end
                               end
                                
                            if ms and ofConcern then
                                local iiName = string.lower(getName(input_item.id))  
                                local ms2, me2 = iiName:find("pure") 
                                if ms2 then
                                    quantity = math.ceil(quantity * boostLevel)
                                    --system.print(" >>> debug >>> " .. tName .. ":" .. iiName .. ":" .. ingredients[input_item.id].quantity .. "=>" .. quantity)
                                    end                                
                                local ms2, me2 = iiName:find("product") 
                                if ms2 then
                                    quantity = math.ceil(quantity * boostLevel)
                                    --system.print(" >>> debug >>> " .. tName .. ":" .. iiName .. ":" .. ingredients[input_item.id].quantity .. "=>" .. quantity)
                                    end
                                end
                            end
    
                        ingredients[input_item.id].quantity = math.max(quantity, ingredients[input_item.id].quantity)
                        local hard_production_cap = 2*2800
                        if ingredients[input_item.id].quantity ~= nil 
                                and ingredients[input_item.id].quantity > hard_production_cap then 
                                ingredients[input_item.id].quantity = math.min(hard_production_cap, ingredients[input_item.id].quantity)
                            end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    until(recurse == false or new == false) 

    return ingredients
end

function addBuild(id, quantity, is_input)
    if id == nil or quantity == nil then
        out("id or quantity can not be nil", id, quantity)
        return
    end
    local new = false
    local key = "" .. id

    if builds[key] == nil then 
        builds[key] = {id= id}
        new = true
    end
    builds[key].quantity = math.ceil(quantity)

    return new
end

function saveTable(name, table)
    databank.clearValue(name)
    local raw = serialize(table)
    databank.setStringValue(name, raw)
    if databank.getStringValue(name) ~= raw then
        out("Unable to save to databank")
        unit.exit()
    end
end

-- ===== MANAGER library part 1: out() prints up to 4 values; getName(id) caches item names (system.getItem is expensive);
-- getPrimaryIngredients(item, recipes) picks the recipe that makes the most of the item and returns its inputs. =====

-- [MEM DEC-005] Old: Lua's garbage collector ran with its defaults (it waits until the heap has DOUBLED before
-- cleaning), so every board sat on a pile of uncollected garbage, and all my boards share ONE memory pool (DEC-002).
-- New: start the next cleaning cycle as soon as the last one ends (pause 100) and clean faster (step multiplier 400).
-- pcall: if the game refuses these options the board still starts. [VERIFY] with tools/memtest/gc_probe.

-- record, which is memory churn in the shared pool. New: they only run when this is true. Set it to true on ONE
-- board while diagnosing, then back to false. (Named tf_debug, not `debug`, so Lua's own `debug` library is untouched.)

function clean(param)
    if param == nil then return " " end
    return param
end

function out(a,b,c,d)
    system.print(clean(a) .. " " .. clean(b) .. " " .. clean(c) .. " " .. clean(d))
end

function getName(id) 
    if id == nil then return "nil Id" end
    if names[id] == nil then
        name = system.getItem(id).locDisplayNameWithSize
        name = name:gsub(" xs$", " XS")
        name = name:gsub(" s$", " S")
        name = name:gsub(" m$", " M")
        name = name:gsub(" l$", " L")
        name = name:gsub(" xl$", " XL")
        name = name:gsub(" product$", " Product")
        names[id] = name
    end
    return names[id]
end

function getPrimaryIngredients(item_id, recipes)
    recipes = recipes or system.getRecipes(item_id)
    if not recipes[1] then return {} end
    
    local primary_ingredients = {}
    local primary_recipe = nil
    local max_produced = 0
    for _, recipe in pairs(recipes) do
        for __, output_item in pairs(recipe.products) do
            if output_item.id == item_id and output_item.quantity > max_produced then
                primary_ingredients = recipe.ingredients
                primary_recipe = recipe
                max_produced = output_item.quantity
            end
        end
    end
    -- [FIX DEC-014] Old: returned only the ingredients; the caller then took the TIME from recipes[1], which may be a
    -- different recipe. New: also return the recipe these ingredients belong to, so time and inputs match.
    return primary_ingredients, primary_recipe
end

-- ===== MANAGER library part 2: serialize / deserialize (tables <-> databank text) =====

local concat = table.concat
local sFormat=string.format

local function internalSerialize(table, tC, t)
    t[tC] = "{"
    tC = tC + 1
    if #table == 0 then
        local hasValue = false
        for key, value in pairs(table) do
            hasValue = true
            local keyType = type(key)
            if keyType == "string" then
                t[tC] = sFormat("[%q]=", key)
            elseif keyType == "number" then
                t[tC] = "[" .. key .. "]="
            elseif keyType == "boolean" then
                t[tC] = "[" .. tostring(key) .. "]="
            else
                t[tC] = "notsupported="
            end
            tC = tC + 1

            local check = type(value)
            if check == "table" then
                tC = internalSerialize(value, tC, t)
            elseif check == "string" then
                t[tC] = sFormat("%q", value)
            elseif check == "number" then
                t[tC] = value
            elseif check == "boolean" then
                t[tC] = tostring(value)
            else
                t[tC] = '"Not Supported"'
            end
            t[tC + 1] = ","
            tC = tC + 2
        end
        if hasValue then
            tC = tC - 1
        end
    else
        for i = 1, #table do
            local value = table[i]
            local check = type(value)
            if check == "table" then
                tC = internalSerialize(value, tC, t)
            elseif check == "string" then
                t[tC] = sFormat("%q", value)
            elseif check == "number" then
                t[tC] = value
            elseif check == "boolean" then
                t[tC] = tostring(value)
            else
                t[tC] = '"Not Supported"'
            end
            t[tC + 1] = ","
            tC = tC + 2
        end
        tC = tC - 1
    end
    t[tC] = "}"
    return tC
end

function serialize(value)
    local t = {}
    local check = type(value)

    if check == "table" then
        internalSerialize(value, 1, t)
    elseif check == "string" then
        return sFormat("%q", value)
    elseif check == "number" then
        return value
    elseif check == "boolean" then
        return tostring(value)
    else
        return '"Not Supported"'
    end

    return concat(t)
end

function deserialize(s)
    return load("return " .. s)()
end
